source_message.text: By default, the level shifter was specified as DNP (Do Not Populate), meaning only its footprint would be on the PCB, with no components soldered. It was included for future-proofing: if a 5V-logic sensor were later attached to the spare I2C0 or UART connectors, the BSS138s could be populated to support it. However, every sensor in our current BOM operates at 3.3V, including SPS30 and ZE08, which are powered by 5V but are compatible with 3.3V logic. Therefore, none of the connected sensors requires the level shifter. You can omit it completely to free up board space. Should we need 5V-logic sensors in the future, we will use a small adapter board instead of permanently reserving footprints.
